title: Having a vector font at the end of a bitmap font fallback chain causes the vector font to override all fallbacks.
body: ### Tested versions **Reproducible in:** * v4.2.1.stable.mono.official [b09f793f5] * v4.3.stable.mono.official [77dcf97d8] * v4.4.stable.mono.official [4c311cbee] * v4.5.beta5.mono.official [c81fd6c51] ### System information Godot v4.5.beta5.mono - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 3 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070 Ti (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.7680) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-10900K CPU @ 3.70GHz (20 threads) - 31.85 GiB memory ### Issue description When there is a dependency chain of fallback fonts longer than two fonts long (i.e. a falls back to b, which falls back to c), having a vector font in the final point of the dependency chain ("c", in the example order) will cause that vector font to completely override all bitmap fonts from the second point ("b") and beyond. Glyphs defined in the first font ("a") will remain unaffected. ### Steps to reproduce n.b. The MRP contains all of these steps done for you, so don't worry about the setup, only the three test cases. 1. Create three bitmap fonts. * The first should be the letter 'a' in a square texture of any size. Configure the image file to import as a font with its character range only having the letter 'a'. * The second should be the letter 'b' in a square texture of any size. Configure the image file to import as a font with its character range having only the letter 'b'. * The third should contain the letters "ab" in a different visual style (to distinguish them). Configure the image to import as a font with its character range set to 'a'-'b'. 2. Configure the properties of 'a' to have one fallback font: The 'b' bitmap font. 3. Create a new scene with a base type of `Label` (or a `Control` scene with a `Label` child). 4. Configure the font overrides of the label so that its font is 'a'. 5. Enter the string "ab" as its text. The 'a' font should render the first character, and the 'b' font should render the second character, as intended. **Test Case 1:** 1. Configure the properties of 'b' to have one fallback font: The 'ab' bitmap font. 2. Upon reimporting 'b', nothing will change with the `Label` instance, as intended. **Test Case 2:** 1. Configure the properties of 'b' to have one fallback font: A new `SystemFont`. 2. Upon reimporting 'b', the label will display a system 'b' in the label, instead of the contents of the 'b' font. **Test Case 3:** 1. Configure the properties of 'b' to have one fallback font: The 'ab' bitmap font. 2. Reimport 'b' to apply changes. 3. Configure the properties of 'ab' to have one fallback font: A new `SystemFont`. 4. Upon reimporting 'ab', a result similar to Test Case 2 will occur where the system font overrides the letter 'b' in the label's display. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [bm-font-bugtest.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21697553/bm-font-bugtest.zip) This test case is for v4.5-beta5. For 4.3 and before, which were also tested, you will need to do the setup manually due to the UID update. The state of this project has Test Case 1 completed already, so testing can be done immediately.
